FICTIONAL TEST DOCUMENT. Ravi Kumar versus State Transport Corporation. The petitioner, a bus conductor, was dismissed from service after a departmental inquiry found that he had issued tickets without collecting fares. The petitioner first approached the Administrative Tribunal, which dismissed his application, and he then filed a writ petition before the High Court, from which this appeal arises. The petitioner argued that the inquiry officer refused to let him cross-examine the ticket checker whose report formed the sole basis of the charge. The court held that denial of the opportunity to cross-examine the only witness against an employee violates the principles of natural justice and vitiates the entire disciplinary proceeding. The dismissal order was quashed. The corporation was given liberty to hold a fresh inquiry from the stage of recording evidence within four months. The petitioner was directed to be reinstated with fifty percent back wages for the period he remained out of service.
